summary.title: Setting Up a Mac Dev Machine From Zero to Hero With Dotfiles
summary.one_liner: You learn how to organize a dotfiles repository and use files like .bash_profile, .osx, .aliases and .gitconfig to automate setting up a macOS developer machine.
keywords: how to set up a new mac for development
takeaways: Store dotfiles in a Git repo and use a bootstrap script to copy them into the home directory, backing up existing files first.
Split configuration into run-once scripts (such as .osx and install steps) and per-session files (such as .bash_profile, .aliases, .functions).
Keep private settings such as .path and .extra out of the public repo, since they can hold sensitive information.
Automate macOS settings with the defaults command, and find new ones by diffing defaults read output before and after a change.
Study existing public dotfiles repos from other developers before building your own.
summary.summary: The article walks through the purpose of each common dotfile on macOS, including .bash_profile, .aliases, .functions, .gitconfig, .inputrc and .osx, with short code examples. It explains how to structure a dotfiles repo, how to use a bootstrap script to link files into the home directory, and how to run the .osx script once. It also covers adding tools such as the z directory jumper, reverting defaults changes, and writing custom .osx commands by diffing defaults output. The tone is informal and the examples use Bash and OS X-era commands (Homebrew, brew cask, Sublime Text).
